symptoms.question: Do you feel vibration mainly at higher speeds (e.g., 80-120 km/h)? (yes/no)
Do you feel vibration already at low speeds (e.g., below 50 km/h)? (yes/no)
Does the steering wheel wobble or shake more when turning? (yes/no)
Do your tyres show uneven wear on the inner or outer edges? (yes/no)

rules.diagnosis: Likely wheel balance or alignment issue.
rules.advice: Vibration at higher speeds often comes from wheel balance or alignment. Driving is usually still possible, but have it checked to avoid uneven tyre wear.

rules.diagnosis: Vibration mainly at low speed can indicate a bent wheel or tyre defect.
rules.advice: Have the wheels and tyres inspected for damage, especially after hitting potholes or kerbs.

rules.diagnosis: Steering wobble when turning can point to worn or loose suspension or steering components.
rules.advice: Have the suspension and steering checked soon to avoid worsening wear or safety issues.

rules.diagnosis: Uneven tyre edge wear usually indicates incorrect wheel alignment or suspension geometry.
rules.advice: Book a wheel alignment check to prevent premature tyre wear and possible pulling while driving.

rules.diagnosis: High-speed vibration together with pulling and uneven tyre edge wear points to wheel alignment and balancing rather than a loose suspension joint.
rules.advice: Drive cautiously and book a wheel alignment and balancing service soon. If pulling worsens or you notice new noises, stop and have the suspension checked.

rules.diagnosis: Vibration at both low and high speeds without pulling or uneven edge wear can indicate an out-of-round tyre or tyre damage.
rules.advice: Inspect tyres for bulges, flat spots, or internal damage and have the wheels checked. Replace damaged tyres before longer trips.
